subject: Post-call: performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - hosted vs current provider
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T15:02:00Z
Subject: Post-call: performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - hosted vs current provider

Alex / team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have a single source of truth. High-level ask from FinLytics: validate end-to-end latency SLOs for your primary generation workloads (short chat snippets and single-turn requests) and compare Hosted Redwood API performance vs your current provider (CloudServeAI).

Recap of the performance targets you mentioned as goals:
- Typical payload: prompt + ~150 tokens output (<=256 token window)
- Target end-to-end (client->response complete): p95 <= 150 ms, p99 <= 350 ms for interactive UX
- Throughput baseline: ~800 req/min (sustained), peak bursts to 2k req/min during batch runs
- Concurrency: expected steady concurrency of ~30-50 sessions; spikes up to 120 concurrent requests during business hours
- Streaming: yes — partial token streaming is required for chat UI; need consistent chunk cadence (max 50ms between chunks at p95 under normal load)

Action items we agreed:
1) Alex: share recent latency dumps and any synthetic load results from CloudServeAI (p50/p95/p99), and any network traces you have for the last 7 days.
2) FinLytics: provide an example request/response pair and a representative traffic shape (concurrency & inter-arrival) we can replay.
3) Redwood (Marissa / Aditya): propose a benchmark plan and run hosted API baseline + controlled comparison to CloudServeAI with the sample traffic. We will run tests at concurrency points: 10, 25, 50, 100.
4) Schedule: target a follow-up on May 20 to review initial numbers; if helpful we can do a joint run live.

Notes / assumptions:
- For "end-to-end" we will measure from client->Redwood edge (TLS) to last token delivered to client (includes network RTT to our public endpoint). If you prefer an internal-only metric, call that out and we will include both.
- If streaming cadence is critical, we will instrument both server-side chunk timing and client-side observed chunk intervals.

Please reply with the artifacts (latency CSVs / traces) and sample request shape. We'll pull together a benchmark doc and share.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-plan.md (coming from our side after Marissa finalizes)
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - hosted vs current provider

Laura — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching the last 3 days of our CloudServeAI synthetic run outputs and a short capture of user-facing latency. Quick notes on our side: 
- Our observed end-to-end numbers (client -> CloudServeAI -> client) for the representative prompt you saw: p50 95 ms, p95 210 ms, p99 490 ms. Numbers vary by region; these are from us-east-1.
- Under sustained high concurrency (>=80) we see occasional amplification of p99 spikes (up to 750 ms) tied to queuing in their autoscaler.
- Streaming: CloudServeAI returns token chunks but chunk spacing becomes uneven under high concurrency; we see intervals up to 220 ms between chunks at p99. That is what's causing the perceived stutter in our chat UI.

I've attached: finlytics-currentprovider-latency-breakdown.csv and netdiag-traces.zip — the CSV includes per-request timestamps and our client-observed chunk intervals. The traces include tcpdump + small app logs from yesterday's peak.

We will also provide the sample traffic shape (JSON) by EOD — it is mostly Poisson-ish inter-arrival with weekday peak between 11:30-13:30.

Thanks — happy to run a live test if Redwood wants to coordinate.

— Alex
Alex Gomez
Performance Lead, FinLytics
alex.gomez@finlytics.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification - hosted vs current provider

Thanks Alex/Laura — received the CSVs & traces. I skimmed the CloudServeAI numbers; their p99 amplification matches what we discussed. Proposed benchmark plan (high level):

1) Baseline: Redwood Hosted API (prod cluster in us-east-1)
   - Workloads: sample prompt with model X (quantized FP16) — match model used in FinLytics example
   - Test points: concurrency [10, 25, 50, 100], sustained for 10 min each; 3 runs per point
   - Throughput: target total request rate per run to approximate your "sustained" 800 req/min and burst shapes
   - Metrics collected: client-observed p50/p95/p99, server-side queue latency, token-chunk interval distribution, CPU/GPU utilization, tail queuing events

2) Comparative run: replay same traffic shape against CloudServeAI (we will coordinate a window) so measurements are consistent (same client location and time window if possible)

3) Streaming cadence test: synthetic stream with fixed token-chunk sizes; measure inter-chunk latency histogram and percentiles at each concurrency point

4) Deliverable: CSVs + consolidated report with charts and recommendation (should include whether we meet your interactive SLOs and suggested configuration changes like batching window, KV cache warmup, or reserved capacity commit suggestions).

Aditya — can you spin up the harness and a quick smoke test against our hosted endpoint today? Please follow the test matrix above and drop raw CSVs into the shared Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/shared/redwood-benchmark-plan. I attached a draft of the runbook (redwood-benchmark-plan.md) with exact commands and query generator config.

Alex — if you can share the traffic JSON today we can aim to run the baseline later today and have initial numbers for the May 20 call.

Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Perfect — thanks everyone. Meeting invite: May 20, 11:00 AM ET to review initial baseline results (I sent a calendar invite). If we can get the FinLytics traffic JSON and the CloudServeAI CSVs in the Drive by EOD today, Marissa & Aditya will run the tests and share results ahead of the call.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/FinLytics — I updated the "Performance Qualification" deal card with the plan and attached docs.

Looking forward to the numbers.

— Laura
